title: #feeds-dev: directories slow to pick up new episodes

messages.text: getting creator complaints again, new eps take like an hour to show up in podcast apps. feed rebuild is finishing in seconds, so this is not on feed-builder.

replies.text: yeah, I checked the last 3 publishes. rebuilds were 4s, 6s, 5s. edge cache is 60s ttl anyway, so once the feed changes it's visible fast.

messages.text: same pattern as before. app shows stale episode list until the directories poll again. we are not holding it anywhere on our side.

replies.text: and WebSub pings are already going out from feed-builder, right?
yep, got the publish logs. ping sent on each feed rebuild. nothing failing there.

messages.text: can we prove the ping path is clean? I want to be able to point creators at something concrete.

replies.text: `kubectl --context prod-eu-west -n feeds logs deploy/feed-builder | grep -i websub | tail -n 5` shows the ping attempts for the last publish.
I can also hit the feed URL directly, it has the new item within a minute. so the delay is after our fetch point.

messages.text: this is mostly the directories' own polling cadence. some of them are near real time, some are not. podcast apps inherit that lag.

replies.text: yeah, and the worst part is creators assume every app behaves like a push system.
we could document it better in the creator help page, but that won't make the directories poll faster.

messages.text: do we have any endpoint or header from the directories that tells us if they accepted the ping?

replies.text: not really reliable across all of them. some ack, some ignore, some poll later anyway. our side only knows the ping left successfully.

messages.text: for what it's worth, I just checked a test show. upload at 14:02, feed rebuild at 14:02:19, app picked it up at 14:57. that's totally in the polling bucket.

replies.text: ok, that lines up with what support is seeing. I'll reply that it's expected propagation, not a broken feed.

messages.text: if we want to improve this, the only lever I see is better creator comms or maybe more aggressive pings, but we already send WebSub on rebuild.

replies.text: agreed. doubling down on pings probably won't change the lag if the directories are just polling on their own schedule.

messages.text: cool, I am not touching any code then. I'll update the reply template to say new episodes usually appear in apps after the directory refreshes, often within a few minutes, sometimes longer.

replies.text: sounds good. maybe mention the feed itself is updated immediately, so they don't keep blaming transcoder or cache.
